abstract.para: Real-time hardware capabilities require predictable response times within a specified margin. This section explains fundamental real-time concepts and the sources of platform interference. It details how to distinguish hardware-induced delays from operating system scheduling overhead using latency tools. Understanding these concepts helps you isolate low-level firmware bottlenecks before deploying production workloads.

topic.para: You must distinguish between hardware-induced and operating-system-induced latencies. The hardware latency detector runs independent of the Linux kernel scheduler. It polls the CPU Time Stamp Counter to find gaps. These gaps indicate when the hardware or firmware disturbed the CPU.
Conversely, cyclictest measures operating system latencies. It runs closer to a real computing situation by including operating system overhead in its results.

In a typical real-time system, the latencies measured with cyclictest should mostly match the latencies from the hardware latency detector. If you detect a significant difference between the two tools, there might be a software bug. In this situation, the operating system causes the latency, and you should contact &suse; for support.
